# About this material {.unnumbered}

This is the written version of the EUSN workshop *Interpreting Model Estimates:
Marginal Effects in RSiena* (11 August 2026), extended so that it can be read on
its own.

It has two halves that do different jobs.

**Chapters 1–2 are for reading.** They set out why a SAOM coefficient is not an
effect size, what a marginal effect is in general, and how the idea has to be
adapted for a model whose decisions are unobserved. Few formulas, and the ones
that appear are the ones you need to read the output later.

**Chapters 3–5 are for running.** They are executable documents, and they scale
up: the worked example computes every quantity from Chapters 1–2 on the `s50` data
that ships with RSiena; Chapter 4 does the same across three school classes and
pools the results; Chapter 5 does it for seventeen classes under six
specifications.

Chapter 6 says which parts are settled and which are current work — worth reading
before relying on any of it in a paper.

## How to use the code chapters

Chapters 3 to 5 are ordinary `.qmd` files and work on their own — open any of them
in RStudio and run the chunks. Chapters 3 and 4 fit their models live and are meant
to be used this way; Chapter 5 reads pre-computed results that ship with the
repository.

The rendered HTML does **not** refit anything: chunk output is cached in `_freeze/`,
which ships too, so the HTML builds in seconds and without RSiena installed. That
cache only affects `quarto render` — running chunks yourself always executes.

```r
remotes::install_github("stocnet/rsiena@sienaMargins")
install.packages(c("metafor", "ggplot2", "sna"))
```

The `sienaMargins` branch is required: `predict()`, `marginalEffects()` and the
target helpers do not exist on the release version. Three things have to be in
place before that install will work:

- **R 4.5.0 or newer.** RSiena has not been compatible with earlier versions
  since 1.5.0.
- **On Windows, [RTools 4.5](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/).**
  The branch ships C++ that is compiled during installation; macOS and Linux
  normally have the compilers already. Either way the build takes a few minutes.
- **The specification syntax introduced in RSiena 1.6.** Everything here is
  written in it. If you know the older syntax, chapter 3 of the manual
  [@SienaManual] sets the old and new function names side by side, and
  `transformScript()` converts a script for you.

## What is in the repository

```
01, 02, 99  the reading chapters (99 is the closing outlook)
03–05       the three executable chapters
data/       where the friendship data go — not included, see data/README.md
scripts/    the meta-analysis pipeline, with its own README
results/    fitted models and per-class marginal effects (.rds)
output/     pooled tables and plots (.csv, .png)
figs/       figures used by the reading chapters
```

The empirical data are not distributed with this material — they belong to the
study they come from. Chapter 4 and `scripts/estimation.R` fetch them on first
use; `data/README.md` says where they come from and on what terms. Chapter 3
needs nothing extra, since it uses the `s50` data that ships with RSiena.

Run anything with the working directory set to the repository root — paths are
relative to it. Opening it as an RStudio project does that for you.

Because every stage's results are included, you can start at any point in the
pipeline: re-pool from `results/postest_all_df.rds` in seconds, recompute
marginal effects from `results/estimation_results.rds` in minutes, or re-estimate
from the raw data if you have the time and have fetched them.
`scripts/README.md` has the run order and the cost of each stage.
